A new report from Counterpoint Research forecasts that consumer wearables will generate more than $1 trillion in cumulative revenue through 2032, led by smartwatches and wireless earbuds. Here are the breakdown details.

Smartwatches and wireless earbuds are expected to lead the market

In a report published today, Counterpoint Research noted that "the global consumer wearables market is projected to surpass $1 trillion in cumulative revenue between 2026 and 2032."

Breaking down the consumer wearables categories, the report forecasts that hearables will account for the largest share of cumulative revenue at approximately $360 billion, followed by smartwatches at $304 billion, and smart glasses at $168 billion.

The following is excerpted from the report:

Health patches are expected to generate an additional $120 billion in revenue, followed by $44 billion for smart rings, $24 billion for neck-worn devices, $18 billion for smart shoes, and $14 billion for fitness bands. Smart socks, smart clothing, and smart belts are each projected to bring in less than $10 billion.

Counterpoint Research noted that revenue growth in consumer wearables is twice as fast as shipment growth, and more notably, the market appears to be gradually shifting from fitness tracking toward preventive health—"where devices alert users to potential issues before they notice them."

Speaking of Apple, the company is already competing in two of the highest projected revenue categories, including AirPods and Apple Watch. Apple is also rumored to be developing smart glasses, while reportedly exploring screen-less fitness bands and smart rings.

Apple last month reported $7.88 billion in revenue for its "Wearables, Home and Accessories" category in the third quarter of fiscal year 2026, representing 6% year-over-year growth and the strongest growth for the category since the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2022.

Although the category clearly covers more than just wearables, Apple's aggressive expansion in this area over the years has become a notable revenue source; Counterpoint estimates that AirPods alone will surpass $100 billion in cumulative revenue by 2026.
